## Available tools 4

Read directly from the server with `tools/list`, grouped by what they act on. If a tool disappears, we record the date.

histor

`histor_check`

Look up an MCP server in HISTOR, a public append-only log of MCP tool sets: when its tool set was first pinned, how often it changed, and what the pattern scan found. HISTOR answers from its own observations and never contacts the server.

tool

`tool_list_cost`

How many tokens an MCP server's tool list adds to every model request, what that costs per 1,000 requests, the heaviest tools, and where it sits among 18,204 packages and 16,170 remote servers. Send a tools/list or name a server HISTOR observes.

warden

`warden_scan`

Scan an MCP server's tools/list with WARDEN, the open-source MCP firewall: static rules and a threat list over every name, description, schema and annotation. Returns allow or block and each finding with its rule and severity. Quoted fragments of the scanned text are left out of the answer.

x402

`x402_check`

Check a signed x402 USDC payment before submitting it: recovers the EIP-712 signer, runs USDC's own checks and the seller's terms, and when the signature fails names the domain it was really made for (e.g. Base Sepolia's 'USDC' used on Base, where USDC is 'USD Coin').

## MCP security checks — WARDEN and HISTOR — questions

Answers built from our own checks of this server.

What can MCP security checks — WARDEN and HISTOR do?

It exposes 4 tools, read directly from the server on our last check. Among them: histor_check, tool_list_cost, warden_scan, x402_check. The full list with descriptions is on this page — we take it from the server itself via tools/list, not from a README. How MCP servers expose tools in the first place →

Is MCP security checks — WARDEN and HISTOR working right now?

We send a real MCP handshake every 15 minutes. Over the last 24 hours 91 of 91 checks got a reply (100.0%), average response time 434 ms. The bar chart above shows every period we have measured.

How do I connect MCP security checks — WARDEN and HISTOR?

Copy the ready config from this page. We generate it for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor and VS Code, each in the form that client actually reads. It is a remote server, so there is nothing to install — the client connects to the address.

Does MCP security checks — WARDEN and HISTOR need an API key?

No. MCP security checks — WARDEN and HISTOR completed a full MCP handshake with us as an anonymous client and listed its tools without asking for anything. All 4 of them are readable on this page. This is what we observed, not what the docs claim.

How fast is MCP security checks — WARDEN and HISTOR?

It answers our handshake in 434 ms on average, which is faster than 30% of all working MCP servers we measure. The comparison comes from our own checks across the whole registry, every 15 minutes.

Is MCP security checks — WARDEN and HISTOR open source?

The code is open source: it is published under the MIT licence, written in TypeScript and 0 stars on GitHub.     Subject: Re: [Dawn] Re: Updated draft-dunbar-dawn-infra-assisted-discovery
    
    Linda,
    
    I reviewed the -03 and have a couple of comments on Caching and Freshness (8.6) and No Result (8.7).
    
      1.  Held Discovery Information: 8.6 says DNS information obtained earlier may still be cached when the requester's Attachment Scope changes, and that a new discovery should use the current context. The Attachment Scope doesn't need to be exposed to the requester (5.3), so it doesn't see its own scope change and nothing prompts that new discovery. Until the TTL runs out, it keeps using what it got under the old scope.
      2.  No Result Versus Error: 8.7 lets a deployment move a subsequent bootstrap operation to a broader scope when one fails to obtain discovery information. DNS-SD's no-result and error indications both count as that failure. A timeout says nothing about whether the edge-local scope has an instance, so falling back on it can hand the requester a less applicable resource.
    We should say in 8.6 that information obtained under an Attachment Scope holds only while that scope holds, and in 8.7 that the fallback follows a complete no-result answer, kept apart from an error.
    
    Thanks,
    Girish
    
    On Sat, Oct 31, 2026 at 10:52 PM Александр Артамохов <alexar76=40rambler.ru@dmarc.ietf.org<mailto:40rambler.ru@dmarc.ietf.org>> wrote:
